issues.description: Zero/nil handling is duplicated across ~20 accessors instead of decomposed into one helper
issues.detail: The same `if f == nil` / `if !x.IsZero()` guard plus empty-slice construction recurs across ir_file.go, ir_type.go, ir_imports.go, and ir_member.go. All three reviewers converge: lift this into one helper (e.g. zeroSafeSlice, or make seq.NewFixedSlice tolerate a zero indexable) so the invariant is stated once. One missed IsZero re-introduces the panic class.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returning -1 invents an in-band sentinel callers will index by and panic
issues.detail: The new postcondition returns -1 for the zero element, but the signature is unchanged and callers doing `e.Value().MessageKeys().At(e.ValueNodeIndex())` will panic on -1. This relocates the failure rather than fixing it. Return `(int, bool)` or an Optional so presence and value are separate.

issues.description: Precondition on nil/zero receivers is never stated; defensive guards substitute for a written contract
issues.detail: Either a zero *File / nil receiver is a legitimate domain value (document it once and enforce at the boundary) or it is a caller bug (let it panic). The PR answers by patching symptoms without deciding. State the invariant — "zero receivers yield empty indexers" — in one place so the next refactor does not re-introduce the panic class.

issues.description: Reflective zero test asserts non-panic rather than a stated specification
issues.detail: zero_test.go enumerates methods with NumIn==1 and checks returns are zero or Len()==0, special-casing ValueNodeIndex and IsZero ad hoc. It proves "does not panic on zero" — a weak invariant — and silently skips non-accessor signatures. A handful of table-driven cases plus a written contract would say more with less reflection machinery.

issues.description: imports.Transitive slice arithmetic preserves an invariant ("last element is implicit descriptor.proto") that is asserted nowhere
issues.detail: `i.files[:max(0, len(i.files)-1)]` silently degrades on the zero/empty path: instead of "exclude the implicit descriptor.proto", it returns whatever is there. Pull the transitive view into a named method on *imports and document the invariant, so the slice arithmetic lives with the data rather than buried inside the zero guard.

issues.description: Symbol.RawData zero-guard lives in export_test.go rather than production code
issues.detail: The IsZero guard for Symbol.RawData was added in the test-export shim. Production callers that reach Raw().data directly remain exposed; if they do not, the test verifies a method the package does not ship. The invariant belongs in the real accessor.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real class of zero-value accessor panics but resolves it by scattering ~20 ad-hoc nil/IsZero guards rather than stating the precondition once. The dominant verdict across Knuth, Hickey, and Dijkstra: lift the pattern into a single helper, decide whether zero receivers are legitimate domain values, and document the invariant. ValueNodeIndex's -1 sentinel merely relocates the panic to callers indexing MessageKeys().At. The reflective zero test proves \"does not panic\" rather than a written contract. Ship-worthy intent, wrong shape — next change in this area will pay the tax again.
